passage:
A student found an online article saying a local festival began in 1920. Another source said 1932.
Instead of choosing the first result, she visited the library archive. Old newspaper records showed that a small version began in 1920, but the official yearly festival started in 1932.
Both dates were partly right.
Her report explained the difference.
The project taught her that research is not always about finding one source and copying it. Sometimes facts have layers.
Good research asks why sources disagree. The answer may reveal a richer story than either source alone.
